primitives.name: Expected Points Added per Play
primitives.verbatim_quote: TEAM EFFICIENCY ### EPA / play (Expected Points Added per play) - **DEFINITION**: Change in expected points from before a play to after it, summed per team/play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'EP_after': 'Expected points after the play (in points)', 'EP_before': 'Expected points before the play (in points)', 'EPA_play': 'Expected Points Added per play (in points)'}
primitives.assumptions: ['The underlying Markov transition matrix for scoring probabilities is stationary across time periods.', 'All plays are conditionally independent given the current state vector (down, distance, field position).', 'The empirical EP distribution is calibrated against historical NFL scoring data.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when a team scores a touchdown immediately after a play, causing a non-differentiable jump in the value function.

layer2.mapping: EPA/play maps directly to the reward signal in a Markov Decision Process (MDP) where states are (down, distance, yard line) and actions are plays. In GSI, this serves as the core conformal prediction target for team scoring outcomes. In GSE, it underpins the state-transition kernel for action-value functions in deep reinforcement learning.
layer2.telemetry: Residual variance between actual team points scored and the sum of EPA/play, which quantifies systematic prediction error.

primitives.name: Success Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Success Rate (SR) - **DEFINITION**: Play succeeds if it gains ≥40% yards-to-go on 1st, ≥60% on 2nd, 100% on 3rd/4th.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'SR': 'Success Rate (dimensionless, percentage)', 'n': 'Total number of plays', 'Indicator_Function': 'Binary indicator (1 if true, 0 otherwise)', 'Threshold_down_i': 'Down-specific yardage threshold (40%, 60%, 100%)'}
primitives.assumptions: ['The yardage thresholds are optimal cutpoints derived from maximizing the correlation between SR and future team wins.', "Each play's success is conditionally independent given the down and distance.", 'The dataset spans multiple seasons to ensure robust statistical calibration.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs at extreme SR values (close to 0% or 100%), where small sample sizes cause high variance.

layer2.mapping: SR is mathematically dual to the probability of exceeding a moving barrier in a Wiener process, providing a direct link to GSI's Bayesian bandit algorithms for player valuation. In GSE, it forms the basis for discrete-state reward shaping in hierarchical policies.
layer2.telemetry: Year-over-year correlation of team SR with subsequent win percentages, serving as an out-of-sample stability test.

primitives.name: DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average)
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) - **DEFINITION**: Team-level VOA adjusted for opponent defense strength and game situation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'DVOA': 'Defense-adjusted Value Over Average (dimensionless, percentage)', 'PlayValue_i': 'Value of the i-th play relative to league average', 'Baseline_i': 'League-average value of the i-th play type', 'TotalPlays': 'Total number of plays in the sample', 'f': 'Adjustment function for opponent defense and game situation'}
primitives.assumptions: ['The adjustment function \\(f\\) is linear in log-odds space to stabilize variance across different defensive strengths.', 'Play values are normally distributed around their mean with constant variance.', 'The sample size is large enough to apply the Central Limit Theorem to the sum of play values.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when the denominator approaches zero, leading to undefined DVOA; this happens during blowout games with few plays.

layer2.mapping: DVOA can be interpreted as a skill-weighted effect size in a hierarchical linear model, aligning it with GSI's conformal prediction intervals for team performance. In GSE, it informs the transition dynamics of policy gradients in adversarial settings.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between DVOA and the log-odds ratio of winning, which measures its predictive power beyond simple win-loss records.

primitives.name: Yardage Equivalent
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **FORMULA**: DVOA = (Σ play_value - Σ baseline_value) / (total_plays) adjusted by opponent-defense average.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'YE': 'Yardage Equivalent (in yards)', 'PlayValue_i': 'Value of the i-th play relative to replacement level', 'AverageYardsPerPlay': 'League-average yards gained per play'}
primitives.assumptions: ['The conversion factor from play values to yards is constant across all teams and seasons.', 'Replacement level is defined as the performance of a freely available backup quarterback.', 'The sum of play values follows a normal distribution centered at zero.']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Regime singularity arises when average yards per play is near zero, causing numerical instability in the division.

layer2.mapping: Yardage Equivalent provides a linear scaling that bridges the gap between DVOA's abstract value metric and physical yardage, enabling seamless integration with GSI's Gaussian process regression for predicting future yardage totals. In GSE, it serves as a reward baseline for contrastive learning of spatial-temporal features.
layer2.telemetry: Mean squared error between predicted YE and actual team rushing yards, used to calibrate the adjustment function.
